The only public function that pays its caller is AegisRewardsV2.claimMerkleRewards(account, cumulativeAmount, proof), and each leaf pays the (account, claimer) pair committed to the current Merkle root - an un-named stranger calling with that leaf reverts InvalidMerkleProof, so a farm bot cannot take existing leaves. All upkeep functions (depositIncome, approve/rejectRedeemRequest, depositRewards, setMerkleRoot, bridgeToChain, sendToStaking) are behind AccessControl roles, and there is no caller fee: the full leaf goes to the named claimer (mostly the user itself or the vault's own keeper). Same architecture verdict as the BSC arm (protocols:562).
